newsitem.title: UK: IGC raises 1996 wheat output, slashes world trade.
newsitem.headline: IGC raises 1996 wheat output, slashes world trade.

text.p: The International Wheat Council (IGC) raised its forecast for the 1996 world wheat harvest by 3.0 million tonnes from its previous estimate to 563 million tonnes.
In its latest monthly report, the IGC saw world wheat trade at 89 million tonnes, down 4.0 million tonnes from last month's figure and the lowest level in the past 11 years.

Higher production and lower demand would allow stocks to recover slightly -- the new estimate for 1996/97 is 101 million tonnes, up 3.0 million from last month and compared with 97 million tonnes in 1995/96.
The new stock figure is the lowest for the past 18 years but signals an improvement from 20 year lows in 1995/96.
"There will be some stock re-building but not to monster levels that we've seen in the 1980s," said Bill De Maria, executive assistant director of the IGC.
The sharp decline in world trade was mainly due to a lower projection for Chinese purchases due to an improvement in local production, the IGC said.
Chinese wheat imports were slashed to 9.0 million tonnes from last month's estimate of 11.5 million while production was raised to 106 million tonnes from 104 million due to reports of better yields.
"China being such a huge market, anything that happens there will have an impact on trade," said De Maria.
As well as China, the IGC saw production increases in the European Union -- currently forecast at 93 million tonnes --, Canada, Russia and Argentina.
But estimates for central and eastern European countries were trimmed due to severe winter conditions. Production in Romania could be slashed by 60 percent from 1995, the IGC said.

The Russian harvest was forecast to increase to 34 million tonnes from from last month's 32.5 million, but forecasts for Kazakhstan and the Ukraine were brought down. --Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 71 510 8072
